text:
ana: seeing a big spike in 502s from hosted inference in us-west-2 starting ~10:12. graphs show high egress latency and connection failures. I think NAT gateway ephemeral ports are getting exhausted after the model-pull burst this morning.

mike: can you paste the error slice / quick logs?

ana: (typo) ana: pasted a short log from API LB -> backend: 
```
[10:12:07] upstream read error: connection reset by peer
[10:12:09] upstream read error: connection reset by peer
[10:12:10] GET https://models.internal.prod:443 -> 502
```

raj: metrics? conntrack? netstat counts?

ana: grabbing node-level stuff now, quick outputs: 
```
$ ss -s
TCP:   sockets: 123456 (estab 3400, closed 110000, orphaned 0, time_wait 91000)
Transport Total     IP        IPv6
RAW     0        0         0
UDP     0        0         0
TCP     123456   82000     41456
```

ana: netstat on a model-puller pod shows tons of TIME_WAIT to s3/model-registry hosts: ~42k TIME_WAIT on :443.

chris: that screams ephemeral port exhaustion. default ephemeral range + many outbound short-lived TLS connections. are model pulls single-connection per model?

mike: checklist:
- confirm NAT gateway metrics (Active connections)
- conntrack table on NAT gateway instances (if nat instance) or VPC counters for NAT GW
- check if we are using S3 VPC endpoints for model artifacts or going over IGW/NAT

ana: NAT GW console for nat-0abc shows ActiveConnections ~53k, and we have 1 NAT GW per AZ. AWS NAT GW is a managed device — once ephemeral ports hit 64k per EIP we see failures.

raj: how many public IPs per AZ? each NAT GW EIP has ~64k source ports. if we have one NAT GW/EIP per AZ we are limited. easiest fix: add extra NAT GW in that AZ (additional EIP) so we multiply port space.

chris: right, or use NAT instances with multiple ENIs/EIPs, but that's more ops. long-term: reduce short-lived outbound connections by enabling connection pooling / keepalive in the SDK and using VPC endpoints for S3.

mike: can we switch model pulls to use S3 VPC endpoint so traffic doesn't hairpin through NAT? that'd remove a bunch of outbound ports.

ana: confirmed: model pulls are hitting s3:// and also third-party model-registry over TLS (registry-host). s3 bucket has no VPC endpoint configured in the cluster VPC.

raj: immediate mitigation options (ordered by speed):
1) create a second NAT GW + EIP in the affected AZ(s). quick and effective but costs ~$0.05/hr + data processing.
2) temporarily throttle model pullers / introduce backoff and jitter in bootstrap to avoid fanout.
3) enable S3 VPC gateway endpoint for the VPC (no data processing fee, no NAT use). needs CFN change and small rollout.
4) shift heavy pulls to dedicated mirror infra inside the VPC (e.g., cache proxies).

ana: tried 2) adding jitter to the rollout — reduced some, but still hitting ceiling when many nodes restart.

chris: also check conntrack table on the NAT GW (if NAT instance) or the VPC flow logs. AWS managed NATGW abstracts conntrack but you can see metrics. if using NAT instances, bump /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max.

mike: cost note: adding NAT GW per AZ increases monthly cost; but data processing charges apply only for NAT GW path. S3 VPC endpoint is cheaper long-term.

ana: quick reproduction test I ran from a pod:
```
for i in {1..20000}; do curl -sSf -o /dev/null https://registry.internal/models/model-x &
done
wait
ss -tan | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
# -> 41000
```

chris: yep. root cause confirmed: fanout of short-lived TLS connections -> TIME_WAIT -> ephemeral port pool exhaustion at NAT EIP level -> downstream resets.

mike: action plan:
- raj: provision extra NAT GW in us-west-2a & 2b now (prod AZs) (P1)
- ana: open PR to add gateway S3 endpoints + rollout plan (P2)
- chris: add a change to model puller to enable HTTP keepalive + pool size + exponential backoff (P2)
- raj: add alert on AWS NAT ActiveConnections > 40k per gateway (P1)

sre-oncall: incident created: INC-2026-184567 (ephemeral-port-exhaustion us-west-2). paging contact list.

deploy-bot: iam-change request created for NAT provisioning (req-4521). tagging owners.

ana: provisioning extra NAT GW now. rolling restart of a small set of nodes to validate reduced 502s.

~20m later~

ana: after adding a second NAT GW per affected AZ and enabling S3 endpoint in the staging VPC test, 502s dropped to baseline. connection counts per NAT GW now ~22k each.

mike: good. longer term we should:
- enforce reuse/keepalive in every service that pulls models (SDK defaults vary)
- implement regional artifact caches behind NLB inside VPC
- consider using EFS / in-cluster cache for hot models
- add proactive alerting on per-EIP active port exhaustion thresholds (ActiveConnections > 50k -> page)

chris: note for docs: include recommended ephemeral port mitigation checklist: 
- use VPC endpoints for heavy S3 traffic
- add per-AZ NAT GW/EIP to scale port space
- reduce connection churn via keepalive / HTTP2 / persistent connections
- avoid node flappy restarts that create fanout pulls
- add model pull rate limits/rolling pulls with jitter

raj: we'll follow up with a small RFC on model distribution architecture (mirrors + VPC caches). I'll own the NAT autoscaling alert.

ana: thanks all, closing thread when monitoring stable. :thumbsup:
